page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Statement
lines: The entropy of a pure, perfectly
crystalline substance is zero at the
steps.why: At 0 K a perfect crystal has exactly one possible arrangement of its particles — perfect order — so its disorder, and therefore its entropy, is zero.
common_mistakes: Dropping pure and perfectly crystalline — a glass or an impure solid keeps some entropy even at 0 K.
steps.memory_tip: Perfect crystal, perfect order: zero kelvin, zero entropy.
steps.margin_note: The three conditions: pure, perfectly crystalline, absolute zero.

steps.label: Mathematical form
steps.why: The limit form states the same law in symbols; the book prints it as Lt S = 0 with T tending to 0.
common_mistakes: Writing ΔS → 0 instead of S → 0 — the law fixes the entropy itself, not a change in it.
steps.memory_tip: Third law gives entropy its zero point, the way sea level gives height its zero point.
steps.margin_note: The limit line completes the answer.

insider_note: This law is the shortest answer in the chapter, so the marks depend on the qualifiers: pure, perfectly crystalline, and 0 K must all appear.
